summary: Marco Rubio participated in a nationally televised Florida Republican primary debate against Charlie Crist, where Crist attacked Rubio over his use of Republican Party of Florida credit cards for personal expenses.
Florida Governor Charlie Crist abandons the Republican Party to run for the US Senate as an independent, setting up a three-way race against Marco Rubio and likely Democratic candidate Kendrick Meek.
Florida senator Marco Rubio announces he is endorsing Mitt Romney for the Republican presidential nomination.
Florida senator Marco Rubio rules himself out as a vice-presidential running mate for Mitt Romney.

Marco Rubio appeared alongside Mitt Romney at a Philadelphia event as speculation intensified over Romney's vice-presidential running mate choice, with both sidestepping questions about a possible partnership.
A model predicts Marco Rubio is the clear favorite to become Mitt Romney's vice-presidential running mate, though ABC reports Rubio is not yet being vetted by the Romney campaign.
Marco Rubio refused to discuss the vice-presidential vetting process during a Meet The Press interview, declining to say whether he was up for the role as Mitt Romney's running mate.
Marco Rubio visited Iowa, giving a campaign-style speech that stirred early talk of a 2016 presidential campaign.
In a GQ interview, Marco Rubio declines to answer how old he thinks the earth is, saying he is "not a scientist, man," and names Jim DeMint and Jeb Bush as admired figures.
Florida senator Marco Rubio will deliver the Republican response to President Obama's state of the union address.
Marco Rubio expressed strong optimism about US immigration reform and fully backed the Gang of Eight draft bill ahead of its publication.
Politico reported that Marco Rubio risks a DC insider label due to his immigration reform push.
Senator Marco Rubio is scheduled to be the headline speaker at the Florida Family Policy Council's annual awards dinner, an event organized by prominent anti-gay activists.

Senator Marco Rubio delivers a speech on the 50th anniversary of the War on Poverty, proposing anti-poverty policies including promoting marriage, block-granting federal poverty programs to states, and emphasizing American optimism.
Marco Rubio releases his book "American Dreams," which is criticized as lacking actual policy innovations despite its emphasis on the word "innovation."
Marco Rubio is reported to be preparing to seek the 2016 Republican presidential nomination, meeting potential donors in Miami to crystallize his plans for a run.

Marco Rubio defended his stance on immigration reform during a question-and-answer session at CPAC, stressing that his objection to Obama's executive action was constitutional rather than policy-based.
Senator Marco Rubio nearly said "nuclear strike" against Iran on Fox News before correcting himself to "military strike," while criticizing President Obama's Iran negotiations.
Marco Rubio declared his intention to run for president, telling donors he feels uniquely qualified, ahead of a rally in Miami.
Marco Rubio laid out a more muscular US foreign policy vision at the Council on Foreign Relations, saying the US is not the "world police" but must intervene more.

Marco Rubio faces renewed scrutiny over allegations that he misused a Florida GOP credit card and treated hundreds of thousands of dollars in political donations to two conservative action committees as a personal slush fund during his time as Florida House speaker.
Republican presidential candidate Marco Rubio was interrupted by immigration activists during a speech at a conservative gathering in Washington.

Marco Rubio denounced Hillary Clinton's claim that the Republican presidential field is hostile toward immigrants as "silly talk," saying enforcing immigration laws is a matter of sovereignty, not hostility.

Marco Rubio concluded a three-day campaign swing through Iowa with seven stops, delivering a message combining domestic and foreign policy with his personal story as a Republican presidential candidate.
Marco Rubio participated in the first Republican presidential debate, where he asserted he had never advocated for exceptions to abortion in cases of rape and incest.

Donald Trump was booed at the Values Voter Summit after calling fellow Republican presidential candidate Marco Rubio "a clown," amid a war of words in which Rubio called Trump a "touchy and insecure guy."
Marco Rubio said President Obama had strengthened Russia's hand by failing to have a clear strategy in the Middle East.
Republican presidential candidate Marco Rubio vows to isolate Russia diplomatically and impose new sanctions on Moscow, calling Vladimir Putin "a gangster and thug."
Republican presidential candidate Marco Rubio raised roughly $6 million in the third quarter of 2015, with about $11 million cash on hand.

Marco Rubio continues to advocate for a piecemeal approach to immigration reform, maintaining he is "personally open" to green cards for undocumented immigrants while emphasizing an enforcement-first process, but declining to specify metrics or timetables for legalization.
Republican presidential candidate Marco Rubio defends his Senate voting absences, saying voting is not the only part of the job.
Marco Rubio received a standing ovation at the North West Iowa Republican Rally, where social conservative attendees expressed openness toward his candidacy.
Marco Rubio's campaign released a full accounting of his use of a Florida Republican Party American Express card, detailing personal charges and repayments.
Marco Rubio participated in the primetime Republican debate in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, where his rising standing among presidential hopefuls was noted despite his relatively low net worth.
Donald Trump said Marco Rubio supports "amnesty" for undocumented immigrants because he is Hispanic.
Marco Rubio signed on to legislation that would delay the implementation of surveillance reforms passed under the USA Freedom Act.
Marco Rubio returned to the campaign trail in Ankeny, Iowa, less than 12 hours after the last Republican debate of 2015, giving a speech focused on his hawkish foreign policy views.
Marco Rubio pressed Ted Cruz on immigration during a Republican presidential debate, accusing Cruz of shifting his position on legalization for undocumented immigrants.

Marco Rubio faced renewed attacks from Republican rivals over skipping Senate votes while running for president, with Chris Christie suggesting he resign his Senate seat and a pro-Jeb Bush Super PAC launching a $1.4m ad buy against him in Iowa.

Marco Rubio framed the presidential election as a choice defining America's global role, criticized Hillary Clinton's record and Republican "isolationist" candidates, and drew responses from Ted Cruz's and Clinton's campaigns.
Marco Rubio wore high-heeled booties while campaigning in New Hampshire, drawing mockery from Republican rivals.

Marco Rubio criticized Republican presidential rivals Ted Cruz and Chris Christie, saying Cruz helped Isis by limiting US surveillance powers and that electing Christie would amount to a third term for Barack Obama.
Marco Rubio accused Ted Cruz of an "intentionally sneaky" tax policy, claiming Cruz's proposed "Business Flat Tax" is a value-added tax that would expand government power.

During a Republican presidential debate, Marco Rubio sidestepped questions about his 2013 immigration bill and recast immigration as a national security issue, saying that if elected president, anyone whose identity or purpose is unknown would not be allowed into the United States.
Marco Rubio said Ted Cruz had misled the American public about his immigration record, maintaining his own record had been clear.
Marco Rubio defied expectations in the Iowa caucuses, finishing strongly alongside Ted Cruz in the Republican primary battle.
Rick Santorum ended his presidential campaign and endorsed Marco Rubio for the Republican presidential nomination.
Marco Rubio defended his repeated debate statements and continued his New Hampshire campaign tour after being criticized for a scripted performance in the Republican debate.
Marco Rubio acknowledged his disappointing performance in the New Hampshire Republican primary, saying "I did not do well" and taking responsibility for the loss.
Marco Rubio campaigned at the Texas Station casino in North Las Vegas, Nevada, ahead of the state's Republican caucuses, with polls showing him at least 20 points behind Donald Trump.
Ted Cruz fired national spokesman Rick Tyler after Tyler promoted a false story questioning Marco Rubio's commitment to the Bible.
Marco Rubio, with assistance from Ted Cruz, attacked Donald Trump's business record and policy acumen during a Republican presidential debate.
Marco Rubio won Puerto Rico's Republican primary, securing all 23 delegates with more than 50% of the vote.
Marco Rubio dismissed rumors that he was considering suspending his presidential campaign before the Florida primary, vowing to stay in the race.
Marco Rubio expressed regret over his personal attacks against Donald Trump, saying he would not do it again.

Marco Rubio admitted during a Fox News town hall that it was a mistake to engage in personal attacks against Donald Trump and refocused on Trump's lack of policy prescriptions, but did not achieve a dramatic moment to revive his campaign.
Marco Rubio condemned Obama's Cuba policy during a Republican debate in Miami, saying the opening had only given the Castro regime more money and that nothing would change for the Cuban people.

At a Republican presidential debate in Miami, Marco Rubio said it is not possible to change the weather or rising oceans through government regulation, drawing criticism from Miami Beach mayor Philip Levine, who said Rubio was “100% using the language of a climate change denier.”
Marco Rubio hedged on whether he would support Donald Trump as the Republican nominee, saying it is "getting harder every day" amid "chaos" and "anarchy."
Marco Rubio won the Republican presidential primary in Washington DC, defeating Donald Trump, John Kasich, and Ted Cruz.
Marco Rubio's presidential nomination hopes were dashed after he lost his home state of Florida to Donald Trump.
Marco Rubio suspended his presidential campaign in March after losing his home state of Florida.
Marco Rubio rules out being a vice-presidential running mate, stating his reservations about Trump's campaign and policies remain unchanged.
Marco Rubio ruled out joining Donald Trump as his running mate, stating he has never sought, will not seek, and does not want to be considered for vice-president.
Marco Rubio says he is willing to speak on behalf of Donald Trump at the Republican convention if asked, while continuing to rule out seeking re-election to the Senate.
Marco Rubio says "maybe" he would run for re-election to his Florida Senate seat if his friend dropped out, an option he had previously foreclosed.
Marco Rubio announced he will seek re-election to a second term in the US Senate, reversing his earlier vows to leave politics after his presidential campaign failed in March.
Marco Rubio denies he has plans for a second presidential bid while saying he will seek re-election to the Senate.
Marco Rubio won the Republican primary for the Florida Senate race, defeating Trump-supporting real estate developer Carlos Beruff.

Democratic congressman Patrick Murphy calls Marco Rubio a "coward" and urges him to withdraw his endorsement of Donald Trump after a leaked 2005 video in which Trump bragged about groping women, but Rubio does not rescind his endorsement.

Marco Rubio and Patrick Murphy squared off in the final debate of their Florida Senate race, during which Rubio responded to Murphy's repeated mentions of Donald Trump by saying "A noun, a verb and Donald Trump: that's his answer to everything."

Senator Marco Rubio announces he will support Rex Tillerson’s nomination for secretary of state despite reservations, allowing the Senate Foreign Relations Committee to approve Tillerson along party lines.
